peiligang-culture.name: Peiligang culture
peiligang-culture.summary: A Neolithic culture in China's Yi-Luo river basin dated to about 7000–5000 BC, known from over 100 sites in a compact area south of the river.

cishan-culture.name: Cishan culture
cishan-culture.summary: A Neolithic culture (6500–5000 BC) in northern China based on millet farming, known for stone tools and distinctive pottery and linked to the origin of Sino-Tibetan languages.

xianren-cave.name: Diaotonghuan
xianren-cave.summary: A rock shelter near Xianren Cave in Jiangxi, China, where some of the world's earliest known pottery, dated to about 20,000-19,000 years ago, was found.

kuahuqiao-site.name: Kuahuqiao site
kuahuqiao-site.summary: Early Neolithic archaeological site near Hangzhou, China, roughly 8,000 years old, linked to an early rice-farming culture.

jiahu.name: Jiahu
jiahu.summary: A Neolithic settlement in central China near the Yellow River, occupied from about 7000 to 5700 BCE, known for early proto-writing symbols, some of the world's oldest playable musical instruments, and evidence of early fermented alcohol.

hemudu-culture.name: Hemudu culture
hemudu-culture.summary: Neolithic culture (5500 to 3300 BC) on the Chinese coast south of Hangzhou Bay; its site, discovered in 1973, revealed stilted lake dwellings unlike northern China's earthen ones.

houli-culture.name: Houli Culture
houli-culture.summary: A Neolithic culture in Shandong, China, dating from about 6500 to 5500 BC, later followed by the Beixin culture.

yangshao-culture.name: Yangshao culture
yangshao-culture.summary: A Neolithic culture along the middle Yellow River in China, roughly 5000 to 3000 BC, marked by advances in agriculture, architecture, and crafts.

banpo.name: Banpo
banpo.summary: A Neolithic site in China's Yellow River valley, representing the first phase of the Yangshao culture (c. 5000-3000 BCE), with circular mud-and-wood houses and communal burials.

longshan-culture.name: Longshan culture
longshan-culture.summary: A late Neolithic culture in the Yellow River valley of northern China, from about 3000 to 1900 BC, noted for its polished black pottery.

ding-vessel.name: ding
ding-vessel.summary: Ancient Chinese ritual bronze cauldrons standing on legs, used for cooking, storage and offerings; owning them became a symbol of royal authority under the Zhou dynasty.

xinglongwa-culture.name: Xinglongwa culture
xinglongwa-culture.summary: A Neolithic culture (6200-5400 BC) in northeastern China known for planned villages with rows of houses, a large central building, surrounding ditches, and jade burial goods.

aohan-banner.name: Aohan Banner
aohan-banner.summary: A banner (administrative division) in southeastern Inner Mongolia, China, bordering Liaoning province and administered by Chifeng City.

chifeng.name: Chifeng
chifeng.summary: A city in Inner Mongolia, China, near the Xinglongwa site, one of the earliest known ditch-fortified settlements.

jiangzhai.name: Jiangzhai
jiangzhai.summary: A Yangshao-culture Neolithic site near Xi'an, China, where the earliest copper artifacts in China were found, and which was fully enclosed by a ring-ditch.

jiahu-symbols.name: Jiahu symbols
jiahu-symbols.summary: Markings carved on tortoise shells and bone found at the Jiahu site in China, dated to around 6000 BCE, seen as possible proto-writing rather than a full writing system.

dawenkou-culture.name: Dawenkou culture
dawenkou-culture.summary: A Chinese Neolithic culture centered in Shandong, lasting from about 4300 to 2600 BCE, known for turquoise, jade and ivory artefacts and early pottery signs.

liangzhu-culture.name: Liangzhu culture
liangzhu-culture.summary: A Chinese Neolithic culture (3300–2300 BC) in the Yangtze River Delta, marked by jade, silk and lacquer elite burials and considered one of China's earliest state societies.

archaeological-ruins-of-liangzhu-city.name: Liangzhu City
archaeological-ruins-of-liangzhu-city.summary: A Neolithic walled city in China, existing from about 3300 to 2300 BCE, thought to be the political and spiritual centre of Liangzhu culture and site of the world's earliest known hydraulic system.

cong-vessel.name: Cong
cong-vessel.summary: A form of ancient Chinese jade artifact, later also made in ceramics.

majiayao-culture.name: Majiayao culture
majiayao-culture.summary: Neolithic culture (3300 to 2000 BC) of China's upper Yellow River region, notable for pioneering agricultural settlement there and for finely painted pottery.

niuheliang.name: Niuheliang
niuheliang.summary: A Neolithic archaeological site in Liaoning, Northeast China, belonging to the Hongshan culture (4700-2900 BC), where a temple, altar and cairn were discovered in 1983.

zhejiang-provincial-museum.name: Zhejiang Provincial Museum
zhejiang-provincial-museum.summary: The provincial museum of Zhejiang, China, in Hangzhou, founded in 1929 and holding over 100,000 items in its permanent collection.

su-bingqi.name: Su Bingqi
su-bingqi.summary: Chinese archaeologist (1909–1997) regarded as the leading theoretician of Chinese archaeology, known for a model of regional cultural development that replaced the idea of culture spreading outward from one core region.

hongshan-culture.name: Hongshan culture
hongshan-culture.summary: A Neolithic culture of northeast China's West Liao river basin, dated about 4700 to 2900 BC, named after a site discovered in 1908 and excavated in 1935.

guo-dashun.name: Guo Dashun
guo-dashun.summary: A Chinese archaeologist, born 1938, known for excavating the Hongshan culture site at Niuheliang and for theories that helped reshape understanding of early Chinese civilisation.

pig-dragon.name: Pig dragon
pig-dragon.summary: A coiled, pig-headed jade artifact made by China's Neolithic Hongshan culture (4700–2900 BC), often placed in graves and possibly an early form of the Chinese dragon.
